Skill to load: tdd-workflow (if unavailable, just follow these rules). Spec (source of truth): `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/.team/notes/spec.md`, section "Server". Use the existing helpers in `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/helpers.mjs` (read it: startServer, runUntilExit, request, postJson, booking, makeTempDir, removeDir, LISTEN_RE, ROOT). Do NOT edit server.mjs, helpers.mjs or anything outside test/startup.test.mjs. Run with `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0 && node --test test/startup.test.mjs` (note: `node --test test/` is broken on Node 22, don't use it). If a test fails because the SERVER violates the spec (not your test), keep the test, and report it to me with the repro; don't weaken it.

Project rules: no console.log; file under 400 lines (split into `startup.test.mjs` and `persistence.test.mjs` if needed); functions under 50 lines; every temp dir removed in finally/after; every started server stopped; assert exact values with assert.equal/deepEqual (never regex/prefix for values the spec names). Use `describe`/`test`.

Tests to write (each one a separate test):
A. PORT (use runUntilExit with DATA_FILE in a temp dir): for each of `+80`, ` 80`, `80 `, `65536`, `1e3`, `0x50`, `-1`, `abc`, `８０` (full-width digits), `99999999999999999999`: exit code 1, stdout === '', stderr matches /^[^\n]+\n$/ (exactly one line) and does not contain 'at ' stack frames / 'Error'. PORT `65535` / `00000`: — for `00000` (all digits, value 0) the server must start (use startServer with env PORT '00000'). Unset PORT: start the server with PORT undefined... skip default-3000 binding test unless port 3000 is free: instead test that empty PORT `''` behaves like unset by checking it does not exit with code 1 within the startup — actually just: spawn with PORT '' and if stdout line is `listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000\n` pass; if it exits with code 1 (3000 in use) check `net` that 3000 is in use and skip via t.skip. Port in use: open a `net` server on 127.0.0.1:0, then run the server with that port → code 1, stdout '', one stderr line.
B. Startup order: PORT invalid AND data file a directory → stderr is NOT `cannot read data file ...` (port checked first), code 1. Data file invalid AND port in use → stderr exactly `cannot read data file <name>\n` (file read before listen).
C. Data file failures, each: exit code 1, stdout '', stderr EXACTLY `cannot read data file ${name}\n` where name is DATA_FILE as given: path is a directory; empty file; `not json`; valid JSON `[]`; `null`; `{}`; a valid store `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}` prefixed with a UTF-8 BOM (bytes EF BB BF); a relative DATA_FILE like `sub/../bad.json` given as relative with cwd = temp dir (stderr must show `sub/../bad.json` exactly, not resolved); a path whose parent is a regular file (`<file>/x.json`, ENOTDIR → exit 1). Also when DATA_FILE is unset and cwd (a temp dir) contains a directory named `bookings.json` → stderr exactly `cannot read data file bookings.json\n`; same with DATA_FILE ''.
D. ENOENT: missing file → starts, GET /api/bookings → `{"bookings":[]}`; missing folder (`<tmp>/nope/deeper/b.json`) → starts; and in both cases the file/folder still does not exist after startup and after GET requests (fs.existsSync false).
E. stdout: after startup and several requests (GET, POST 201, POST 400, DELETE 204, 404), then stop, the whole stdout === `listening on http://127.0.0.1:${port}\n` exactly, and the port is a number > 0.
F. Relative DATA_FILE resolved against cwd: spawn with cwd = temp dir, DATA_FILE = 'rel.json', POST a booking → file `<tmp>/rel.json` exists, and no `rel.json` in the repo root. Also DATA_FILE unset with cwd = temp dir → POST creates `<tmp>/bookings.json`.
G. File not written at startup or on GET/failed POST/failed DELETE: write a valid store file, record its exact bytes and mtimeMs; start; GET /api/rooms, GET /api/bookings, POST invalid (400), POST 415, DELETE /api/bookings/99 (404), GET / ; stop; bytes identical and mtimeMs unchanged. Also: with a missing file, failed POSTs don't create it.
H. Persistence: start, POST 3 bookings (ids 1,2,3), DELETE 3 and DELETE 2, stop, restart with same DATA_FILE → GET shows only booking 1 with identical fields; next POST gets id 4. Also delete ALL bookings, restart, next id continues (not 1). The memory is the truth: after startup, overwrite the file externally with `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}` content changed — GET still shows the old bookings.
I. Save failure: DATA_FILE = `<tmp>/folder/b.json` with folder missing → POST valid booking → status 500, json deep-equal `{"error":"internal error"}`, content-type exactly `application/json; charset=utf-8`; GET /api/bookings → `{"bookings":[]}`; server still running; then mkdir the folder, POST again → 201 with id 1 (next id unchanged); folder not created by the server before you mkdir it (check existsSync false after the 500). Also a DELETE save failure: start with a valid store in `<tmp>/d/b.json` holding one booking id 1 (nextId 2), then rm -rf `<tmp>/d` while running, DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 500 internal error, GET still shows the booking; recreate dir, POST → id 2.
J. Spec says the server writes nothing to stdout except the line, and the file content is JSON the server can read back: after a POST, `JSON.parse(readFileSync(file))` succeeds.

Report back: file(s) written, test count, pass/fail output summary, and any server spec violations found (with exact repro).

content.content: 1 # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions allowed) 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. I wrote the startup and persistence tests, and all 40 pass against the current `server.mjs`. I found no server spec violations.

The `tdd-workflow` skill wasn't available, so I followed your rules directly.

**Files**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/startup.test.mjs` has A (PORT), B (startup order), C (unreadable data file), D (missing file or folder) and E (stdout). It has 25 tests.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/persistence.test.mjs` has F (relative `DATA_FILE`), G (no writes), H (persistence), I (save failure) and J (file content). It has 15 tests. I split the work because one file would have been over 400 lines.

**Run:** `node --test test/startup.test.mjs test/persistence.test.mjs` gave 40 tests, 40 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.

**Choices where the spec left room**
- **Skip case:** the "empty PORT means 3000" test would skip itself if port 3000 were in use. It ran and passed here.
- **Stack-trace check:** A rejects a stack-trace line (`/^\s+at /m`) and any `Error` in stderr, instead of checking for the bare text `at `, which could appear in a friendly message.
- **B, port first:** the first test also asserts that stderr contains no `cannot read data file` at all.
- **Extra check in E:** E also matches the stdout against `LISTEN_RE`.
- **Extra check in J:** J also asserts stdout holds only the listening line.
- **Coverage trimmed in H:** the "delete all, restart" case in H seeds three bookings, deletes them all, restarts, and expects the next id to be 4.

Every temp dir is removed in `finally`, and every started server is stopped in `finally`.
